sections.heading: What Is Low-E Glass and Why Does It Matter for Tysons Properties?
sections.body: Low-emissivity, or Low-E, glass features a microscopically thin metallic coating applied to the glass surface. This coating reflects infrared energy while still allowing visible light to pass through, which means your building stays brighter without gaining or losing as much heat through the glass. For the densely developed commercial district surrounding Tysons Corner Center and the growing mixed-use developments along Route 7, managing solar heat gain is a practical concern that affects occupant comfort year-round. In winter, Low-E coatings help retain interior heat; in summer, they reduce the burden on cooling systems. Property managers overseeing Class A office space, retail storefronts, or residential condominiums near the Silver Line Metro stations consistently find that upgrading to Low-E glazing addresses comfort complaints from tenants and occupants. Our team can assess your existing window and curtainwall systems and recommend the appropriate Low-E product type — whether hard-coat or soft-coat — based on your building's orientation, use, and existing frame conditions.

sections.heading: The Installation and Replacement Process Explained

faq.q: What is the difference between hard-coat and soft-coat Low-E glass?
faq.a: Hard-coat Low-E glass has its metallic coating applied during the glass manufacturing process, making it more durable and easier to handle. Soft-coat Low-E glass has the coating applied after manufacturing and is typically sealed inside an insulated glass unit to protect it. Soft-coat products generally offer stronger thermal performance characteristics, while hard-coat is valued for its durability. Our team can help you determine which type is best suited for your specific application.

faq.q: Can Low-E glass be installed in my existing window frames?
faq.a: In many cases, yes. If your existing frames are structurally sound and in good condition, we can often fabricate a replacement insulated glass unit with a Low-E coating to fit your current frame. This approach avoids the cost of full window replacement. However, very old or damaged frames may need to be replaced at the same time. We assess frame condition during our on-site evaluation and give you an honest recommendation before any work is scheduled.
